candidate_relations.reason: BCIE (classic epidermolytic hyperkeratosis) shares the same histopathology and KRT1/KRT10 mutations but presents with generalized erythroderma and diffuse hyperkeratosis. The clinical record specifically documents annular hyperkeratotic plaques (Figure 1A), which define AEI as a separate subtype. BCIE does not capture the annular morphology that is the defining feature of AEI.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Bullous Congenital Ichthyosiform Erythroderma (BCIE/EHK) is the classic generalized form of epidermolytic ichthyosis; AEI is a distinct, rarer subtype characterized by annular/circinate lesions rather than diffuse erythroderma

candidate_relations.reason: The candidate correctly identifies the molecular etiology (KRT1 mutation causing epidermolytic hyperkeratosis) confirmed by WES c.482T>C (p.L161P) in KRT1, and the histopathology is consistent. However, it does not specify the annular subtype (AEI), which is the required diagnostic specificity given the annular plaques documented clinically and in Figure 1A. The label is a parent/broader category missing the annular subtype designation.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Epidermolytic Hyperkeratosis due to KRT1 mutation is the mechanistic/etiologic parent category; AEI is a specific clinical subtype within this group defined by its annular morphology

case_quality_flags: AEI is a rare, well-defined subtype of epidermolytic ichthyosis; the annular morphology is the key distinguishing feature from classic BCIE/EHK
KRT1 c.482T>C (p.L161P) is a known pathogenic variant associated with AEI specifically
